title: Heimdall prefetch station: adaptive host prefetch & affinity scheduler to cut CPU-GPU contention
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Host-side overhead (CPU cycles, memcpy spikes, and threadpool contention) is a dominant contributor to tail latency for short-sequence and bursty prefill workloads. Current prefill/decode staging creates many small host->GPU memcpy operations, frequent task wakeups on the host threadpool, and suboptimal NUMA placement for KV cache slices. Kernel selection and attention-mode mismatches amplify pressure on the host by increasing coordination events and reducing batching efficiency.

Goal: Implement an adaptive host-side "prefetch station" and affinity-aware scheduler (codename Heimdall) that: 1) coalesces prefill memcopies into staged blits with size/latency tradeoff heuristics; 2) assigns prefetch workers with NUMA/GPU affinity to reduce cross-socket traffic; 3) moves kernel selection hints earlier and groups compatible requests to increase kernel reuse and attention-mode locality; and 4) throttles background prefetches based on observed GPU queue depth and token pacing. Target metric: reduce host CPU cycles per token by >=30% and reduce p99 end-to-end latency for 1–32 token prefill workloads by >=20% in our standard benchmark.

Scope: Prototype scheduler in host runtime, integrate with existing staging buffer abstraction, add heuristics for coalescing thresholds, and expose a runtime flag and console metric for adaptive behavior. Provide backward-compatible fallback to existing scheduler.

Acceptance criteria: 1) End-to-end microbench harness shows >=30% reduction in host wall-time per token for the short-seq workload on c6g-like instances; 2) p99 latency improvement >=20% for bursty prefill tests; 3) no regression (>3%) in long-sequence throughput; 4) metrics surfaced in Console (per-route host_cpu_per_token, memcpy_coalesce_rate, numa_migrations); 5) feature gated with rollout toggle + canary policy.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Bench harness (bench/pre_fill_short.yaml) shows >=30% reduction in median host CPU per token and p99 latency drop >=20% vs baseline; 2) No throughput regressions >3% on long sequences (512+ tokens); 3) Console exposes new metrics memcpy_coalesce_rate, host_prefetch_backpressure, affinity_hit_rate; 4) Canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on error rates >1% or latency regressions; 5) Documentation and release notes updated.
risks_mitigation:
Risk: Over-coalescing increases latency for low-concurrency requests. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds + dynamic backpressure based on observed GPU queue latency.
Risk: NUMA pinning may interfere with container scheduling. Mitigation: respect cgroup cpu sets and provide env flag to opt out in constrained envs.
Risk: Kernel selection hints might diverge from runtime decisions. Mitigation: hinting only used to group candidates, final kernel selection still validated in GPU runtime; fall back path maintained.
comments: 2025-10-10 - Asha Patel: Initial triage and hypothesis: memcpy fanout and thread wakeups are dominant in short-seq profiles. Collected perf traces (FlameGraphs) for 50K requests; attached to design doc.

2025-10-18 - Marco Li: Spike implemented a simple coalescer in a feature branch. Local perf: host CPU/token down 18% but single-request median latency up ~6% under single-threaded test. Added backpressure to avoid tail regressions.

2025-10-25 - Eng Review (Sophie Nguyen): Reviewed heuristics. Suggested adding affinity fallback when cgroup cpuset is set and exposing metric for affinity_hit_rate. Also asked for unit tests around coalescing boundary conditions.

2025-11-02 - Marco Li: Integrated NUMA-aware worker pool and added kernel-hint grouping mechanism. Bench harness run against rio-4 cluster: median host cycles/token improvement 34%, p99 latency down 23% for short-seq. Added canary rollout plan.

2025-11-08 - QA (Diego Ramos): Stability tests: 72h soak under mixed load. Observed two small GC-related spikes in the scheduler thread under extreme concurrency; added retry/backoff and monitoring alert.
2025-11-10 - PM (Lina Ortiz): Approved canary. Added label and schedule for runtime-1.20 release notes.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal canary on staging cluster (5% traffic) with runtime flag heimdall_enabled=false by default; 2) Enable heimdall_enabled=true + monitor for 48h; if stable, expand to 25% traffic; 3) After 7d stable, 100% rollout with console switch to force-off in case of regressions; 4) Post-rollout: 1-week watch, collect perf traces, and follow-up tidy up (remove debug logs).
notes: Prototype focused on integer token batched prefetch paths first, then extend to attention-mode-aware grouping for kv-cache shapes. Keep gesture towards kernel selection improvements by emitting grouping metadata consumed by the GPU runtime. Avoid changing existing ABI.
